user_story: As a writer, I want a default document to open when I visit the app and a stable URL per document, so that I can land in an editor immediately and bookmark/share specific docs.
expected_behaviour: The home route ('/') renders EditorWorkspace with documentId=DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_ID ('demo-document'). The dynamic route '/doc/[id]' normalizes the URL param via normalizeDocumentId() (lowercases, replaces non [a-z0-9-] with '-', collapses/strips dashes, caps at 96 chars, falls back to 'demo-document' if empty) and mounts EditorWorkspace keyed on that id so navigation between docs fully remounts the workspace. EditorWorkspace is dynamically imported with ssr:false (client-only mount). Page-level <main> has role=main, an sr-only h1 'Lash Collaborative Editor', and a section labelled 'Document editor'.

user_story: As a writer, I want to create a new blank document with one click, so that I can start fresh work without leaving the editor.
expected_behaviour: Clicking the 'New document' button (Icon 'plus', data-testid='new-document-button') calls handleCreateDocument: it generates a unique id via createNewDocumentId() ('doc-<base36 time>-<8-char uuid/random>', normalized), upserts it into localStorage with title 'Untitled document', refreshes the document list, and navigates (router.push) to documentPath(nextDocumentId) ('/doc/<id>').

user_story: As a writer, I want to see and switch between my documents from a dropdown, so that I can navigate my workspace.
expected_behaviour: A <select> (aria-label 'Open document', data-testid='document-open-select') lists documents from listDocuments(localStorage). The list always includes the 'demo-document' pinned first, then other records sorted by updatedAt descending; each option's value is documentPath(id) and label is the stored title. The active document is always present in the options (synthesized if missing). Changing the select calls router.push to the chosen path. Documents are loaded on mount and the active doc is upserted into the registry when activeDocumentId changes.

user_story: As a writer, I want to rename my document inline and have the name persist, so that documents are identifiable across sessions and tabs.
expected_behaviour: A text input (aria-label 'Document title', data-testid='lash-doc-title-input') is bound to docTitle state, initialized from readDocumentTitle(localStorage). On change it updates state and calls saveDocumentTitle() (writes 'lash:title:<id>' key, upserts registry record, normalizes empty -> 'Untitled document') then refreshes the list. On blur it normalizes/persists again. The browser tab title is set to '<title> — Lash' whenever docTitle changes.

user_story: As a writer, I want a rich-text editor that loads with my document's extensions and shows a loading state, so that I can edit content reliably.
expected_behaviour: useEditor() mounts a TipTap editor with createLashEditorExtensions() configured per-document (outline persistence keyed to documentId via localStorage, image uploader, optional Yjs collaboration when realtime enabled, link prompt handler, doc-chip resolver), autofocus 'end', immediatelyRender:false. Until isMounted && editor are ready a 'Preparing your editor…' placeholder is shown; then EditorContent renders with class 'lash-editor-content'. Editor editability is toggled via setEditable based on invite access scope. The workspace remounts (key=documentId) per document so editor state is isolated.

feature: App shell layout (sidebar / topbar / canvas / rail grid)
user_story: As a user, I want a consistent workspace layout with navigation chrome around my document, so that tools are organized and predictable.
expected_behaviour: AppShell renders a CSS grid container ('lash-app') hosting sidebar, topbar, a focusable canvas ('lash-canvas', tabIndex=-1) wrapping the document, and the rail (only when railOpen). It sets data attributes (data-focus-mode, data-rail-open, data-sidebar-collapsed, data-mobile-drawer, data-rail-mobile, data-entrance) that drive CSS for collapse/focus/responsive behavior. On first mount a transient data-entrance='true' flag is set for 800ms then cleared to run entrance choreography once. A backdrop button closes any open mobile drawer.

feature: Left sidebar with navigation, outline, and collapse
user_story: As a user, I want a collapsible left sidebar with nav links and a live document outline, so that I can navigate sections and reclaim space.
expected_behaviour: Sidebar shows brand, a static PRIMARY_NAV (Current doc[active], Home, Inbox, Starred, Shared with me) and SECONDARY_NAV (All documents, Settings) as non-functional buttons, plus a live outline (OutlinePanel) from outlineItems. A footer collapse toggle (data-testid='sidebar-collapse-toggle', aria-pressed) flips sidebarCollapsed; when collapsed an 'Outline' access button (data-testid='sidebar-outline-access') re-expands it. Outline is hidden entirely when focus mode is on. Clicking an outline heading focuses/scrolls the editor (handleFocusHeading); the disclosure toggles heading collapse (handleToggleHeading). Note: nav links are presentational only (no onClick/routing).
errors: [ux/medium] Outline and collapse work: collapse toggle flips sidebarCollapsed (aria-pressed), the collapsed 'Outline' access button re-expands, outline is hidden in focus mode, and outline clicks focus/scroll the editor or toggle heading collapse. However PRIMARY_NAV (Current doc, Home, Inbox, Starred, Shared with me) and SECONDARY_NAV (All documents, Settings) are rendered as buttons with NO onClick handler — pure dead controls. 'Current doc' even carries aria-current='page' and data-active, presenting a non-functional control as the active nav target. This is misleading affordance for a shipped UI.

feature: Top bar chrome (title, focus/suggest toggles, share, avatars, mobile menu)
user_story: As a user, I want a sticky top bar exposing document state and quick actions, so that key controls are always reachable.
expected_behaviour: TopBar shows the doc icon + title, an AutosaveIndicator, a focus-mode toggle (data-testid='focus-mode-toggle', aria-pressed, swaps maximize/minimize icon), a suggest-mode toggle (data-testid='suggest-mode-toggle', aria-pressed, flips isSuggestMode adding a 'Suggesting' meta badge), a Share button (data-testid='topbar-share-button') that opens the Share rail tab, a static 3-avatar collaborator stack (Apollo/Ada Lovelace/Grace Hopper), and a mobile menu button that opens the mobile sidebar drawer. The 'extras' slot injects the document open-select + new-document button. Note: the avatar stack is hardcoded, not derived from live presence.
errors: [ux/medium] TopBar shows doc icon+title, AutosaveIndicator, focus-mode toggle (aria-pressed, maximize/minimize swap), suggest-mode toggle (aria-pressed, drives the 'Suggesting' meta badge), a Share button that opens the Share rail tab, a mobile menu button, and the extras slot (document select + new-doc button). All wiring is correct. The defect is the 3-avatar collaborator stack: it is hardcoded (Apollo/Ada Lovelace/Grace Hopper) with title='<name> · viewing now', presenting fake live presence as real. A separate, genuinely live presence bar (realtimePresence) exists near the document header, making the top-bar stack redundant and actively misleading.

user_story: As a user, I want an activity rail organized into jumpable sections, so that I can reach chat, history, AI, sharing, and activity panels.
expected_behaviour: RightRail renders chip buttons (Chat, History, AI, Share, Activity) over a scrolling column where all five panels are siblings. Clicking a chip calls onChange and smoothly scrolls to that section (respecting prefers-reduced-motion); an IntersectionObserver updates the active chip to whatever section is most visible, with a 400ms scroll-lock after a click and a -40% bottom rootMargin to suppress overscroll false fires. The History chip shows a badge with the version count. A close button (when provided) closes the rail.

feature: Panel toggling via keyboard shortcuts (focus mode, rail)
user_story: As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts to toggle focus mode and the activity rail, so that I can manage screen real estate without the mouse.
expected_behaviour: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F toggles isFocusMode (listener skipped on coarse-pointer/touch devices to avoid hijacking iOS keyboard); focus mode sets data-focus-mode on the shell, hides the toolbar and outline. Cmd/Ctrl+/ toggles railOpen. Both ignore IME composition (keyCode 229), key repeat, and call preventDefault. The top-bar focus-mode button and the handleFocusModeToggle callback also toggle the same state.

feature: Mobile drawers for sidebar and rail
user_story: As a mobile user, I want the sidebar and activity rail to open as overlay drawers with proper focus handling, so that the app is usable on small screens.
expected_behaviour: On narrow widths the sidebar/rail become slide-in drawers controlled by mobileSidebarOpen/mobileRailOpen. Opening stashes the trigger element so focus returns to it on close; Escape closes any open drawer (AppShell key handler); a backdrop click closes drawers; while a drawer is open the canvas is marked 'inert' (no tab/AT reach) and the body is scroll-locked via position:fixed at the negative prior scrollY (restored on close). Opening the Share panel on <=767px also opens the mobile rail drawer.

user_story: As a writer, I want to toggle bold, italic, underline, and inline code on my selection, so that I can emphasize and format text inline.
expected_behaviour: Clicking the Bold/Italic/Underline/Code toolbar buttons (or invoking runToolbarCommand with id 'bold'|'italic'|'underline'|'code') runs editor.chain().focus().toggleBold()/toggleItalic()/toggleUnderline()/toggleCode().run(), which adds the mark to the current selection if absent or removes it if present. Each is rendered as an icon button in the 'Inline formatting' (marks) group.

user_story: As a writer, I want to convert the current block to/from a heading level 1, 2, or 3, so that I can structure my document.
expected_behaviour: Clicking Heading 1/2/3 (ids 'heading-1'|'heading-2'|'heading-3') runs editor.chain().focus().toggleHeading({ level }).run() with level 1, 2, or 3, converting the current block to that heading or back to a paragraph if it is already that heading level. Rendered in the 'Structure' (blocks) group.

user_story: As a writer, I want to toggle bullet, numbered, and checkbox lists, so that I can organize items.
expected_behaviour: Bullet List runs toggleBulletList(), Ordered List runs toggleOrderedList(), and Checklist runs toggleTaskList() (the 'checklist' id maps to TipTap's task list). Each wraps/unwraps the current block(s) in the corresponding list type. Rendered in the 'Structure' (blocks) group.

user_story: As a writer, I want to insert a default table, so that I can add tabular content.
expected_behaviour: Clicking Insert Table (id 'insert-table') runs editor.chain().focus().insertTable({ rows: 3, cols: 3, withHeaderRow: false }).run(), inserting a 3x3 table with no header row at the cursor. Because it is an insertion (not a toggle), its active state always returns false.

feature: Link set/unset with URL prompt and normalization
user_story: As a writer, I want to add or remove a hyperlink on my selection by entering a URL, so that I can link to external resources.
expected_behaviour: Clicking the Link button calls handleLinkCommand, which reads the existing link href, opens window.prompt('Link URL', currentHref). Cancel (null) aborts. An empty/whitespace result runs runToolbarAction(editor,'link') with no href, which calls unsetLink() (extendMarkRange('link').unsetLink()). A non-empty value is normalized (http(s)/mailto kept as-is, otherwise prefixed with 'https://') then setLink({ href }) is applied over the extended link mark range. Active state = editor.isActive('link').

user_story: As a user, I want toolbar buttons to visually indicate when the current selection has that formatting, so that I know the active state.
expected_behaviour: For each button, isToolbarButtonActive(editor, id) maps to editor.isActive('bold'/'italic'/'underline'/'code'/'link') or editor.isActive('heading',{level}) or isActive('bulletList'/'orderedList'/'taskList'); 'insert-table' is always false. The EditorToolbar sets data-active, aria-pressed, and (in ToolbarButton) applies a blue highlight style when active. Buttons are disabled until an editor instance exists (disabled={!ready}).
errors: [a11y/low] Active-state mapping is correct in isToolbarButtonActive (toolbar.ts:34-63): each id maps to the right isActive() check and insert-table is always false. The live toolbar (panels/EditorToolbar.tsx:80-95) renders bare <button class='lash-icon-btn'> with data-active and aria-pressed, NOT the ToolbarButton.tsx component, so the inline activeStyles in ToolbarButton.tsx:23-26 is dead code; the active highlight depends entirely on a CSS rule. That CSS rule DOES exist (globals.css:836-840: .lash-icon-btn[data-active='true'],[aria-pressed='true'] sets coral background/color), so the highlight is functional — it is just driven by CSS, not by ToolbarButton.tsx. Secondary a11y issue: aria-pressed='false' is set on the insert-table action button (EditorToolbar.tsx:90), which is not a toggle, so a screen reader announces it as an unpressed toggle, which is semantically inaccurate.

feature: Toolbar grouping, icons, and shortcut tooltips
user_story: As a user, I want toolbar buttons grouped with icons and keyboard-shortcut tooltips shown per platform, so that the toolbar is discoverable.
expected_behaviour: Buttons are split into 'Inline formatting' (marks) and 'Structure' (blocks) groups via toolbarGroups. Each renders an SVG Icon (COMMAND_ICONS map) falling back to a text glyph. The hotkey string is converted by shortcutHint to a per-platform label (Mod->Ctrl/Cmd, Alt->Opt, Shift symbol) and shown as title/data-tooltip e.g. 'Bold (Ctrl+B)'. These hotkey strings are DISPLAY metadata only; actual keystroke handling relies on the underlying TipTap mark/heading/list extensions' built-in keymaps, and the Link 'Mod+K' label has no wired keybinding to the prompt flow.
errors: [spec-error/medium] Grouping, icons, and tooltips are correct: toolbar.ts:13-26 tags each button group=marks/blocks; EditorToolbar.tsx:29-42 maps all 12 ids to IconName values that all exist in components/shell/Icon.tsx (IconName union lines 34-45: bold/italic/underline/code/link/h1/h2/h3/list-bullet/list-numbered/list-check/table), with a text-glyph fallback (EditorToolbar.tsx:94); shortcutHint (EditorToolbar.tsx:44-53) builds per-platform tooltips. The story's expected_behaviour is mis-derived: it claims hotkeys are display-only and that Mod+K is not wired to the prompt flow. In reality LashKeyboardShortcuts (base.ts:61-85) explicitly wires Mod-b/i/u/e, Mod-Alt-1/2/3, Mod-Shift-8/7/x/t, and Mod-k. Mod-k (base.ts:76-82) calls this.options.onRequestLink when present, i.e. it IS wired to the prompt flow. Separately chip.ts:431-441 ALSO binds Mod-k, returning false when no chip is at the selection so it falls through to the link handler; this shared keybinding is fragile and undocumented.
notes: SPEC-ERROR: story expected_behaviour to be corrected per audit. Spec-corrected: code is intentional; the story expected_behaviour was over-claimed (see DEFERRED.md/ERRORS.md). No code defect.

user_story: As a document author, I want each heading to receive a stable identifier, so that outline collapse state and navigation can reliably target the right section.
expected_behaviour: On any transaction that changes the doc, an appendTransaction plugin walks all heading nodes; any heading lacking a `headingId` attr gets one derived from its position as `heading-${pos.toString(36)}` via setNodeMarkup. The heading attribute is defined on the LashHeading extension (default null) and serializes to/from the DOM as `data-heading-id`. Headings without an assigned id are also given a positional fallback `heading-${pos}` in outline computation.

user_story: As a writer, I want a structured outline of my document headings, so that I can see and navigate the document hierarchy.
expected_behaviour: computeOutlineItems scans the doc for heading nodes and produces an ordered OutlineItem[] each carrying headingId, level (default 1), title (textContent or fallback `Heading N`), collapsed flag, descendantCount (count of consecutive deeper headings), hiddenBlockCount (doc-level blocks between this heading and the next same/higher-level heading), and from/to/contentFrom/contentTo positions. getOutlineItems exposes the list. The OutlinePanel renders an ordered list, indenting entries by (level-1)*1.1rem and showing a meta label `{descendantCount} sections · {hiddenBlockCount} blocks`. EditorWorkspace republishes the outline on doc/selection changes, deduping with sameOutlineItems.

user_story: As a writer, I want to collapse a heading to hide its content, so that I can focus on document structure.
expected_behaviour: toggleHeadingCollapse(headingId) toggles the id in the collapsedIntent set and dispatches a 'set-collapsed' meta transaction. Collapsed sections produce hidden ranges (contentFrom..contentTo) which become `lash-hidden-block` node decorations on every block in range, visually hiding section content. The OutlinePanel toggle button shows ▶ when collapsed / ▼ when expanded, sets aria-expanded and data-collapsed, and calls onToggle which routes to lashCommands.toggleHeadingCollapse. isHeadingCollapsed/getCollapsedHeadingIds expose collapse state.

user_story: As a writer, I want to expand every collapsed heading at once, so that I can quickly reveal the entire document.
expected_behaviour: expandAllHeadings command checks the collapsedIntent set; if empty it returns true as a no-op, otherwise it dispatches a 'set-collapsed' meta with an empty collapsedIds array, clearing all collapse state including ids for headings not currently present in the doc.
errors: [ux/medium] The expandAllHeadings command logic is correct and matches the story's acceptance criteria: at outline.ts:321-339 it reads pluginState.collapsedIntent (the unfiltered intent set, not the doc-filtered visible `collapsed` set), no-ops returning true when the intent set is empty, and otherwise dispatches a 'set-collapsed' meta with collapsedIds:[] which clears all collapse state including ids for headings no longer present in the doc. The command is exposed via lashCommands.expandAllHeadings (commands.ts:60-68). However, it is NOT wired to any user-facing affordance: a grep of apps/web and packages for expandAllHeadings / 'Expand all' / 'expand-all' returned only the two definition sites (commands.ts and outline.ts) and zero callers. OutlinePanel.tsx:25-29 renders only an <h2> 'Outline' title in its header (no expand-all button); the toolbar config (toolbar.ts) has no expand-all entry. A returning user with collapsed sections can only expand them one at a time. The user story's goal ('expand every collapsed heading at once') is unreachable through the UI.

user_story: As a writer, I want my cursor moved out of a section when I collapse it, so that the caret never lands inside hidden content.
expected_behaviour: When a heading is collapsed, findNextVisiblePosition locates the first heading whose `from` is at/beyond the collapsed range's contentTo (skipping nested children) and the selection is moved there via PMSelection.near(resolved, 1). If no following visible heading exists, the caret falls back to a position inside the still-visible collapsed heading itself (min(target.from+1, doc.content.size)) to avoid searching backward into hidden content.

user_story: As a returning user, I want my collapsed sections to survive page reloads and content re-loads, so that my document view stays consistent.
expected_behaviour: The plugin tracks two sets: collapsedIntent (every id the user collapsed, even if absent from the current doc) and collapsed (intent ∩ current heading ids, used for decorations/UI). On apply, when a set-collapsed meta arrives or the intent set changes, it saves Array.from(collapsedIntent) via the persistence adapter; on init it loads ids for the documentId. The web app wires createLocalStorageOutlinePersistence(window.localStorage) keyed by activeDocumentId, storing JSON under `lash-outline:{docId}`. A memory adapter (Map-backed) is also provided. localStorage adapter guards against undefined storage and catches/logs JSON errors, returning [] on failure.

user_story: As a writer, I want to click an outline entry to jump to that heading, so that I can navigate long documents quickly.
expected_behaviour: The OutlinePanel jump button (aria-label `Jump to {title}`) calls onFocus(item). EditorWorkspace's handleFocusHeading chains focus().setTextSelection({from: item.from, to: item.from}).scrollIntoView(), placing the caret at the heading start and scrolling it into view.

user_story: As a writer, I want to import a Markdown file into the editor, so that I can bring existing Markdown content into a Lash document.
expected_behaviour: parseMarkdownToDoc(markdown) parses text via unified+remark-parse+remark-gfm and walks the mdast tree. It converts headings (clamped to levels 1-3), paragraphs, bullet/ordered/task lists (start attr preserved for ordered), tables, and inline marks (bold->strong, italic->emphasis, inlineCode->code mark, links with href). Reference-style image and link definitions are collected into a definitions map and applied. Hard breaks become hardBreak nodes. Empty input yields a doc with a single empty paragraph. Returns { doc: JSONContent, warnings: string[] }.

user_story: As a writer, I want GFM tables in my Markdown to import as editable tables, so that tabular data survives the import.
expected_behaviour: convertTable maps each mdast TableRow to a tableRow; the first row becomes tableHeader cells and subsequent rows tableCell, each with attrs { colspan:1, rowspan:1, colwidth:null }. Cell inline content is converted (allowImages=true) and wrapped via ensureParagraph so each cell holds at least one paragraph. Produces a ProseMirror 'table' node.

user_story: As a writer, I want to be warned when Markdown features can't be fully represented, so that I understand what changed on import.
expected_behaviour: Unsupported/lossy nodes add deduplicated warning strings: code blocks become plain paragraphs, blockquotes are flattened, thematic breaks (HR) are removed, HTML blocks/snippets are stripped, strikethrough (delete) becomes plain text, images inside headings become alt text, and missing image reference definitions warn. Warnings are returned as an array. In the UI (EditorWorkspace.showWarnings) non-empty warnings are console.warn'd and shown via window.alert.

user_story: As a writer, I want to export my document to Markdown, so that I can use it outside Lash.
expected_behaviour: serializeDocToMarkdown(doc) converts the ProseMirror JSON to mdast and stringifies via remark-stringify with options { bullet:'-', fences:true, listItemIndent:'one' } plus remark-gfm. Handles headings (depth clamped 1-3), paragraphs, bullet/ordered/task lists (ordered start preserved, task checked state), tables, and inline marks (bold->strong, italic->emphasis, link->link, code mark->inlineCode). Underline marks export as emphasis with a warning. Images are emitted as reference-style images with collected definitions appended to the document root. Returns { markdown, warnings }.
errors: [bug/low] In serializeDocToMarkdown, convertTableToMdast extracts each table cell's inline content via cell.content?.[0]?.content (index 0 only), so it reads only the inline children of the FIRST block of a cell. If a table cell contains multiple paragraphs or a non-paragraph block (a user can create a second paragraph in a cell with Enter), the additional blocks are silently dropped with no warning, causing data loss on export. Code-block export is also unhandled (no codeBlock case in convertDocNodeToMdast, lines 472-516; unsupported nodes fall to the default branch and emit an empty paragraph + 'Unsupported node' warning), but code blocks are not in the schema so that part is genuinely minor.

user_story: As a writer, I want images preserved across Markdown export, so that image references aren't lost.
expected_behaviour: On export, convertImageToMdast deduplicates images by src, assigns ids like 'image-N', emits imageReference nodes (referenceType 'full'), and appends matching definition nodes (identifier/label/url) to the document root so remark-stringify produces reference-style image syntax with link definitions. On import, those definitions are resolved back to inline image nodes (src/alt).

feature: Import .md file via toolbar button + hidden file input
user_story: As a user, I want an Import button that lets me pick a .md file and load it, so that importing is a one-click action.
expected_behaviour: The MarkdownIO toolbar renders an upload icon button (data-testid markdown-import-button) that calls onImportClick, which clicks a hidden file input (accept='.md,text/markdown'). On file change, handleMarkdownFileChange reads file.text(), clears the input value, runs parseMarkdownToDoc, replaces editor content via editor.commands.setContent(doc, false), and surfaces warnings.

feature: Export .md file download via toolbar button
user_story: As a user, I want an Export button that downloads my document as Markdown, so that I can save it locally.
expected_behaviour: The MarkdownIO download icon button (data-testid markdown-export-button, disabled when exportDisabled) calls onExportClick. handleExportMarkdown serializes editor.getJSON(), shows warnings, stashes the result on window.__lashLastExport (for tests), then creates a Blob (text/markdown), an object URL, and a temporary anchor with download='document.md' that is clicked to trigger the download, then cleaned up.

user_story: As a writer, I want typing Markdown shorthand (e.g. '# ', '- ', '1. ', '**bold**') to auto-format, so that I can format without the toolbar.
expected_behaviour: Markdown shorthand is provided by TipTap input rules, not custom code in this cluster: StarterKit supplies bullet list ('- '/'* '), ordered list ('1. '), inline code (backticks), bold ('**'), and italic ('*') rules, and LashHeading (extends TipTap HeadingExtension, levels 1-3) supplies the '#'/'##'/'###' heading rule. These are wired via createLashEditorExtensions in schema/base.ts. No Lash-specific markdown input-rule code exists; behaviour is inherited from the configured extensions.

user_story: As a document author, I want to assign a cell type of text, status, or select to table cells, so that I can capture structured data like task status alongside free text.
expected_behaviour: Each table cell carries cellType ('text'|'status'|'select'), value, and options attributes. setSelectionCellType (wired via lashCommands.setTableCellType) updates every selected cell: switching to 'text' clears options and restores the prior value as paragraph text content; switching to 'status'/'select' applies provided options or, when none are given, falls back to defaults (status: Todo/In Progress/Done; select: Option A/B/C). Cell attrs persist to HTML as data-cell-type / data-cell-value / data-cell-options (options JSON-encoded) and round-trip back via parseHTML. The node view sets display value to the stored value if it is in the option list, else the first option. Non-text cells hide their contentDOM and show a control button.

user_story: As a document author, I want to pick or cycle through the allowed values of a status/select cell, so that I can quickly set a cell's value from its option set.
expected_behaviour: cycleSelectionCellOption (lashCommands.cycleTableCellOption) advances/retreats the value of each non-text selected cell through its resolved options with wraparound (clampOptionIndex uses modulo). setSelectionCellValue (lashCommands.setTableCellValue) sets a cell's value; for text cells it also rewrites paragraph content. The DOM node view renders a listbox menu of option buttons; clicking an option commits that value and closes the picker. The TableCellPanel React surface shows current value chip, Cycle/Back buttons, and an option grid that calls setValue on click.

feature: Keyboard navigation of status/select cell picker
user_story: As a keyboard user, I want to open and navigate a cell's option picker with Enter/Space/arrows/typeahead, so that I can set cell values without a mouse.
expected_behaviour: A ProseMirror plugin (createLashTableInteractionPlugin) handles keydown on non-text cells with options. When closed: Enter (no shift) or Space opens the picker at the current value's index. When open: ArrowDown/ArrowRight moves to next option, ArrowUp/ArrowLeft to previous (wraparound), Enter commits the active option and closes, Escape closes without committing, Tab commits the active value and lets the event propagate (returns false) so focus moves on, and any single printable character does typeahead-selecting the first option that startsWith that letter. Picker open state, active index, and option count are tracked in plugin state and reflected via aria-expanded / data-active / aria-selected on the DOM; open position is remapped through doc changes.

feature: TSV copy of table cell selection
user_story: As a document author, I want to copy a range of selected table cells, so that I can paste the data into spreadsheets or elsewhere as tab-separated values.
expected_behaviour: On copy, if there is a table cell selection, handleCopyEvent builds a matrix from the selected rect via extractSelectionMatrix (using each cell's display value: text content for text cells, the value attr for status/select), serializes it to TSV with buildTsvFromMatrix (tabs between columns, newlines between rows), prevents the default copy, and writes the same TSV to both text/plain and text/tab-separated-values clipboard formats.
errors: [ux/medium] TSV copy works for a true cell range: handleCopyEvent builds a matrix via extractSelectionMatrix (text content for text cells, value attr for status/select), serializes with buildTsvFromMatrix, preventDefaults, and writes both text/plain and text/tab-separated-values. However hasTableSelection returns true whenever the caret merely sits inside any cell (collectSelectedCells uses cellAround for non-CellSelection and returns the single surrounding cell). So pressing Ctrl/Cmd+C with just a caret — or a partial text selection inside one cell — is hijacked: the entire cell is copied as TSV and the native copy is prevented, clobbering normal in-cell text copy.

feature: TSV/CSV paste into table cell selection
user_story: As a document author, I want to paste tabular data into a selected table region, so that the cell values are filled in from my clipboard.
expected_behaviour: On paste with a table cell selection, handlePasteEvent reads text/tab-separated-values (or falls back to text/plain), parses it via parseClipboardTableText: lines split on tabs if any tab is present, otherwise on commas, with values trimmed and rows normalized to equal column counts. applyMatrixToSelection maps the parsed matrix onto the selected rect cell-by-cell (positions remapped through the transaction): text cells get their paragraph content replaced; status/select cells accept the pasted value only if it is a valid option, else fall back to the first option. If any cell changed, default paste is prevented and any open picker is closed.
errors: [ux/medium] Paste logic is correct: handlePasteEvent reads text/tab-separated-values (falls back to text/plain), parseClipboardTableText splits on tabs if any tab present else commas, trims, normalizes ragged rows to equal columns, and applyMatrixToSelection maps cell-by-cell with positions remapped through tr.mapping.map; text cells get paragraph content replaced, status/select cells accept only valid options else fall back to options[0]; on change it preventDefaults and closes any open picker. Same over-broad gating issue as copy: hasTableSelection is true for a mere caret in a cell, so pasting clipboard text while just typing in a single cell is intercepted and the value is force-overwritten/normalized instead of inserting at the caret.

user_story: As a document author, I want to type a phrase like "next Friday 3pm" after @, so that I can insert a structured date mention without manually picking a date.
expected_behaviour: parseDateMention(input, ctx) lowercases/trims the input and matches the regex /^next\s+(\w+)(?:\s+at)?\s+(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm)?$/. It supports weekday names sunday..saturday, an optional "at", a 1-2 digit hour, optional :MM minutes, and optional am/pm. If the string does not match the pattern or the weekday is unknown, it returns null. On match it resolves the NEXT occurrence of that weekday (strictly in the future: distance = (weekday - today + 7) % 7 || 7, so the same weekday today maps to 7 days later). 12-hour normalization: "pm" with hour<12 adds 12; "am" with hour==12 becomes 0. Returns a visible date mention {visible:true, kind:'date', refId:`date:<iso>`, display, iso}. Example: input 'next Friday 3pm' with now=2026-05-16 yields iso '2026-05-22T15:00:00+09:00' (Asia/Tokyo).

So offsets are only correct for the two hard-coded zones; all other IANA zones silently emit a 'Z' (UTC) offset even though the display below uses the real timeZone, producing a mismatch for unsupported zones.

Navigating between /doc/identity-alpha and /doc/identity-beta shows each doc's own title; a fresh doc shows DEFAULT_DOC_TITLE 'Untitled document'. document-identity.spec.ts verifies titles stay isolated across two routes and survive reload.

user_story: As a user, I want each document to live at a stable, clean URL, so that I can bookmark and share it reliably.
expected_behaviour: normalizeDocumentId lowercases, replaces non [a-z0-9-] runs with '-', collapses/trims dashes, caps at 96 chars, and falls back to DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_ID ('demo-document') when empty. documentPath(id) yields /doc/<normalizedId>. The /doc/[id] route and / home route both normalize the id and key EditorWorkspace on it. The current route is displayed in doc metadata (data-testid lash-doc-route). After creating a doc the URL matches /doc/doc-[a-z0-9-]+ and the route text persists across reload.

user_story: As a user, I want to create a fresh document with one click, so that I can start writing without leaving the app.
expected_behaviour: A '+' button (data-testid new-document-button, aria-label 'New document') in the TopBar extras calls handleCreateDocument: createNewDocumentId() generates `doc-<base36 time>-<8-char uuid/random>` normalized, upserts it into the registry with DEFAULT_DOC_TITLE, refreshes the document list, and router.push navigates to documentPath(newId). Verified by document-identity.spec.ts (button click navigates to /doc/doc-... and route persists after reload).

user_story: As a user with several documents, I want to switch between them from a dropdown, so that I can navigate my workspace quickly.
expected_behaviour: A <select data-testid="document-open-select" aria-label="Open document"> in the TopBar lists registry records (listDocuments). Options are sorted with the demo doc first, then by updatedAt descending; each option label is the doc title and value is documentPath(id). The active doc is injected into options if not yet in the registry. Selecting an option fires handleOpenDocument -> router.push to that path. document-identity.spec.ts confirms selecting registry-alpha navigates there and restores 'Registry Alpha' title.

user_story: As a returning user, I want my documents remembered, so that the switcher reflects everything I have worked on.
expected_behaviour: listDocuments seeds a 'demo-document' record, merges parsed records from localStorage key lash:documents (parseRegistry tolerates malformed/non-array JSON by returning []), overlays each record's live title via readDocumentTitle, and sorts demo-first then updatedAt-desc. upsertDocument writes/updates a record (preserving createdAt, bumping updatedAt) and rewrites the registry. refreshDocuments and a storage-change effect re-read the list into React state so the switcher stays current.
errors: [spec-error/low] listDocuments seeds demo-document, merges parsed records (parseRegistry tolerates malformed/non-array JSON by returning []), overlays live titles, and sorts demo-first/updatedAt-desc; upsertDocument preserves createdAt and bumps updatedAt. However the story claims 'a storage-change effect re-reads the list into React state so the switcher stays current' — there is NO window 'storage' listener for the document registry (lash:documents). The only storage listener is for suggestion resolutions. So the switcher updates only on local mutations (create/title-edit via refreshDocuments) and not on cross-tab registry changes.
notes: Cross-tab doc switcher sync added (storage listener on lash:documents / lash:title:*).

user_story: As a user, I want a left navigation rail with brand and section links, so that I can orient myself within the workspace.
expected_behaviour: Sidebar renders a 'Lash' brand block plus a static PRIMARY_NAV ('Current doc' marked active with aria-current=page, Home, Inbox, Starred, Shared with me) and SECONDARY_NAV ('All documents', 'Settings'). Each NavItem is a <button> with an icon, label, and title tooltip, but no onClick handler — they are presentational placeholders that do not navigate anywhere.
errors: [ux/medium] Sidebar renders the 'Lash' brand plus PRIMARY_NAV (Current doc [active, aria-current=page], Home, Inbox, Starred, Shared with me) and SECONDARY_NAV (All documents, Settings). Each NavItem is a <button> with icon+label+title but NO onClick handler — they are non-functional presentational placeholders. They look like real navigation but do nothing when clicked, which is a UX trap (dead controls presented as live). The story's expected_behaviour explicitly acknowledges this stub state, so it matches the code, but it remains a real UX gap for end users.

feature: Sidebar collapse / expand with outline re-access
user_story: As a user, I want to collapse the sidebar to gain space yet still reach my outline, so that I can focus without losing navigation.
expected_behaviour: The workspace defaults to the collapsed icon rail on desktop. An Outline access button (data-testid sidebar-outline-access) remains in the collapsed sidebar, while the canonical live OutlinePanel renders beside the document canvas as lash-document-outline / lash-outline-panel at wide desktop widths. SidebarOutline renders only when the sidebar is expanded or the mobile drawer is open, using sidebar-specific test IDs to avoid duplicate canonical outline landmarks. In focus mode the document outline is omitted. sidebar-regression.spec.ts verifies collapsed access, visible document-side outline jumping, expansion fallback, mobile drawer close/focus restore, and adjacent outline/a11y specs verify collapse, persistence, caret movement, and screen-reader navigation.
notes: OUT follow-up: document-side outline now primary on desktop; collapsed global nav remains icon-only.

feature: Mobile sidebar drawer with focus restoration
user_story: As a mobile user, I want to open and close the navigation drawer, so that I can navigate on small screens without losing my place.
expected_behaviour: On mobile a TopBar hamburger (data-testid topbar-mobile-menu, aria-label 'Open navigation menu') calls handleOpenMobileSidebar, stashing event.currentTarget and opening the drawer (AppShell data-mobile-drawer='true'). The Sidebar then renders a close button (data-testid sidebar-mobile-close) that calls closeMobileSidebar, which closes the drawer and refocuses the stored hamburger trigger. sidebar-regression.spec.ts confirms drawer open/close and focus returns to topbar-mobile-menu.

user_story: As a user, I want a scroll-synced activity rail, so that I can jump between document-side panels and always know which section I'm viewing.
expected_behaviour: RightRail renders all tab panels as stacked sections in a scrolling column plus a chip nav (aria-label 'Jump to activity section'). Clicking a chip (data-testid rail-tab-<id>) calls onChange and scrollIntoView (smooth, or 'auto' under prefers-reduced-motion) to that section, arming a 400ms scroll-lock. An IntersectionObserver (threshold 0.25/0.5/0.75, rootMargin bottom -40%) keeps the active chip in sync with the most-visible section, respecting the lock window. Chips show a badge (capped '99+') when badge>0, use aria-current on the active chip, and an optional close button fires onClose.

feature: TopBar document chrome (title display, autosave, presence, share)
user_story: As a user, I want a sticky header showing my doc title, save state, collaborators, and a share action, so that I have at-a-glance document context and controls.
expected_behaviour: TopBar shows a document icon + read-only title text (topbar-doc-title), an AutosaveIndicator, focus-mode and suggest-mode toggle buttons (aria-pressed, swapping icon/label), an AvatarStack of three hard-coded present collaborators (Apollo/Ada Lovelace/Grace Hopper with 'viewing now' titles), and a Share button (topbar-share-button, aria-expanded/aria-controls=lash-rail) that opens the share rail. The collaborator stack is static demo data, not live presence.
errors: [ux/medium] TopBar shows a document icon + read-only title text (topbar-doc-title), AutosaveIndicator, focus/suggest toggles (aria-pressed, swapping icon/label), an AvatarStack, and a Share button (aria-expanded/aria-controls=lash-rail) opening the share rail. The collaborator stack is HARD-CODED demo data (Apollo/Ada Lovelace/Grace Hopper, all 'viewing now'), shown as if live presence. Real presence exists elsewhere (realtimeSnapshot.peers in EditorWorkspace), so the static avatars are misleading fake data.

user_story: As a user, I want a metadata line under the title, so that I can see authorship, version count, sections, route, and access at a glance.
expected_behaviour: Below the title input a metadata row (data-testid lash-doc-meta) renders: 'Edited by Apollo' (hard-coded), pluralized version count from historyEntries.length, pluralized section count from outlineItems.length, the current route via documentPath(activeDocumentId) (lash-doc-route), and an invite/access status string (Owner access / Access granted:<scope> / Denied:<reason>). title-edit.spec.ts also asserts the title stays above the meta box on mobile (no overlap).
errors: [ux/low] The metadata row (data-testid lash-doc-meta, aria-label 'Document metadata') renders 'Edited by Apollo' (HARD-CODED, not derived from real authorship), pluralized version count (historyEntries.length), pluralized section count (outlineItems.length), the live route (documentPath via lash-doc-route), and the invite/access status (Owner access / Access granted:<scope> / Denied:<reason>). All values are real except the authorship line, which is a static placeholder presented as factual metadata.

feature: Route an insight to a writing place
user_story: As a writer, I want to send a selected insight (selection, AI answer, note, chat message, or todo) to a chosen destination, so that valuable content lands in the right system instead of being lost in the doc.
expected_behaviour: InsightRouter.route(payload, placeId) validates the payload, enforces idempotency, runs the place accepts guard, isolates per-place write errors, records an audit entry, and returns a typed WriteResult {ok,placeId,ref|code,error,at}.
notes: Hardened core router.

user_story: As a writer, I want default destinations for an insight, so that I can insert it, spin it into a new doc, or copy it without extra setup.
expected_behaviour: createDocumentInsertPlace/createNewDocumentPlace/createClipboardPlace register builtin places that are always configured; the host supplies the effectful handler; write returns a ref.
notes: Host wires handlers in EditorWorkspace (Phase 3 UI).

user_story: As a writer, I want to save an insight to Persephone memory, so that it becomes long-term recallable knowledge.
expected_behaviour: createPersephonePlace(client?) registers an external place. Unconfigured by default: route returns {ok:false, code:unconfigured} with the actionable PERSEPHONE_UNCONFIGURED message. With a PersephoneClient.remember() it returns {ok:true, ref:persephone:<id>}.
notes: Placeholder adapter; supply PersephoneClient to wire.

user_story: As a writer, I want to dispatch an insight to a Hermes agent, so that it can be acted on autonomously.
expected_behaviour: createHermesPlace(client?) registers an external place. Unconfigured by default returns code=unconfigured + HERMES_UNCONFIGURED. With HermesClient.dispatch() returns ref:hermes:<taskId>.
notes: Placeholder adapter; supply HermesClient to wire.

user_story: As a writer, I want to turn an insight into a todo in garden-state/gardenos, so that follow-ups become tracked tasks.
expected_behaviour: createGardenPlace(client?) registers an external place. Unconfigured by default returns code=unconfigured + GARDEN_UNCONFIGURED. With GardenClient.createTask() returns ref:garden:<id>.
notes: Placeholder adapter; supply GardenClient to wire.

user_story: As a developer, I want malformed insights rejected with clear errors, so that bad data never silently reaches a writing place.
expected_behaviour: validateInsightPayload checks id, kind (enum), non-empty text, docId, ISO createdAt, and range invariants. route() returns code=invalid with the joined error list; nothing is written.
notes: No silent fallback (CLAUDE.md).

user_story: As a writer, I want re-sending the same insight to the same place to be a no-op, so that I never create duplicates.
expected_behaviour: An (payload.id+placeId) pair is written at most once; repeat routes return the prior success flagged idempotent:true without invoking the handler again.
notes: stableInsightId derives content-based ids.

user_story: As an operator, I want a failing destination to fail only itself and be logged, so that routing stays reliable and traceable.
expected_behaviour: A place whose write throws is caught and surfaced as code=failed; the router never auto-redirects. Every attempt (success/failure) is appended to history() with payloadId, placeId, kind, result, timestamp.
notes: No cascade; append-only audit.

user_story: As a writer, I want the UI to show which destinations are ready, so that I am not offered places that cannot accept my insight.
expected_behaviour: availabilityFor(payload) returns each place with available + reason, reflecting isConfigured() and the accepts() guard.
notes: Drives the Send-insight menu.
